summary: Hemchandra Raychaudhuri was an Indologist and historian. He served as Carmichael Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta, where his tenure is attested in 1939 and 1965.
Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri worked in linguistics and Indology, holding a professorship at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1991 and 2026).

Hendrik Kern studied at Utrecht, Leiden (doctorate under Antonie Rutgers), and under Albrecht Weber. He taught at Athenaeum Maastricht (1858–1862), Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1863–1865), and held the Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1865–1903).

Henepola Gunaratana studied at Kelaniya, Buddhist Missionary College, and American University (BA and PhD). He led the Buddhist Institute of Kuala Lumpur (~1958–1968) and held posts at the Buddhist Vihara Society, American University, Georgetown, Bucknell, and Maryland.

Heng Sure studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union (PhD under Ronald Y. Nakasone), as well as under Hsuan Hua. He has held professorships at the Graduate Theological Union, Bond University, and Dharma Realm Buddhist University.

Henk Blezer studied at Leiden University (Doctoraal 1987–1997). A scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, he worked at Leiden University (postdoctoral researcher 1993–1997; lecturer 2002–2008) and the International Institute for Asian Studies (1997–2001).

Henk Bodewitz earned classical, Indo-Iranian, and doctoral degrees at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He held posts at Utrecht University (assistant professor 1966; chair of Sanskrit 1976–1992) and Leiden University (associate professor ~1973–1976; professor 1992–2002).

Henri Bergson was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Condorcet, École Normale Supérieure (~1878–1881), and the University of Paris. He taught at the lycée David d'Angers (~1881–1883) and the Collège de France (1900–1904).

Henri Cordier, who studied at Lycée Chaptal, worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He served as a professor at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1881–1925) and at Sciences Po (~1885–1925).

Henri Gaidoz studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber. He taught geography and ethnography at Sciences Po (1872–1908) and served as directeur d’études for Celtic philology at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from 1876.

Henri Hubert studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and École Normale Supérieure (~1892–1895). He held appointments at the National Archaeological Museum (~1898–1927), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901–1927), and École du Louvre (~1906–1927).

Henri Lévy-Bruhl studied under Marcel Mauss. He held academic posts at the Université de Lille Faculté de droit (1919–1929), the Paris Law Faculty (~1930–1955), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1957–1964).

Henri Maspero studied under Édouard Chavannes and at INALCO and EFEO. He worked at EFEO, Maison Franco-Japonaise (1928–1930), and held chairs in Sinology at the Collège de France (1918–1945), University of Paris, and Sorbonne University.
Henri Massé worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the University of Algiers (~1916–1927) and at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1927–1958).
Henri Pirenne was a historian who studied at the University of Liège (~1879–1883). He served as Professor of History at Ghent University from 1886 to 1931.

Henrik Samuel Nyberg studied at Uppsala University, beginning in 1908. He taught at Fjellstedt School (~1916–1919) and served as Dozent and Professor of Semitic languages at Uppsala University (~1919–1956).
Henrik Zilliacus, a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology, studied at the University of Helsinki (~1926–1936) and later held an academic post there (~1944–1974).
Henry Beveridge studied at the University of Glasgow and Queen's University Belfast. He worked in the Indian Civil Service (1857–1893) and served as President of the Asiatic Society (1890–1891).

Henry C. H. Shiu works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Toronto (completed by 2006), having studied under Shek-Wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David B. Waterhouse, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby.

Henry Clarke Warren was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Harvard (A.B. ~1875–1879), Johns Hopkins, and Oxford, under teachers including Charles Rockwell Lanman, Maurice Bloomfield, and Thomas William Rhys Davids.
